# Tasks: Evaluating Statistical Fidelity of Synthetic Data Generation Techniques

**Inputs**: `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/spec.md`, `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/plan.md`, data model and metric-results contract.

**Research question**: To what extent do summary statistics, correlation structures, and distributional shapes in synthetic tabular datasets generated by CTGAN, DP-GAN, and CopulaGAN faithfully reproduce those of the original real datasets?

This is a research implementation plan targeting the smallest complete study: three real tabular benchmarks, three generators, three seeds, full fidelity metric suite (including Fisher's z-transformed correlation deviations per constitution Principle VI) with multiplicity correction, sensitivity analysis, and a reproducible report. All compute is CPU-tractable (SDV generators run on CPU; datasets down-sampled under the RAM monitor per FR-009). Output paths follow the plan's project layout (`src/`, `outputs/`, `data/`, `tests/`, `contracts/`).

## Task format and paths

Use `- [ ] T### [P?] [USx?] description with exact artifact paths`. Paths are relative to the project directory. The canonical contract path used throughout is `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/contracts/metric_results.schema.yaml` (per plan.md Project Structure). Tasks editing the same file are sequential; independent files run in parallel only where marked `[P]` and only when their verification does not depend on another task's outputs.

## Phase 1: Setup and first end-to-end analysis

- [X] T000 [US1] Write a pinned dependency file `requirements.txt` at the project root covering every dependency with exact versions: `sdv==1.12.0`, `ctgan==0.5.2`, `torch==2.2.0` (CPU wheel), `pandas`, `numpy`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`, `statsmodels`, `datasets`, `openml`, `matplotlib`, `seaborn`, `pyarrow`, `pytest`, `jsonschema` (pin each to the version resolved at authoring time). This implements plan Phase 0 and constitution Principle I (reproducibility: pinned dependencies, isolated virtualenv). Verify: `python -m venv /tmp/fresh-venv && /tmp/fresh-venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt` succeeds in a clean environment, and `pip check` reports no broken dependencies.
- [ ] T001 [US1] Implement real-data loading and preprocessing in `src/data/loader.py` for the three verified datasets: Adult via OpenML (`openml.datasets.get_dataset(1590)`), UCI-HAR via `datasets.load_dataset("udayl/UCI_HAR", split="train")`, and UCI-Shopper via `datasets.load_dataset("jlh/uci-shopper", split="train")`. The loader MUST fail loudly (raise) on any fetch failure — no synthetic/mock fallback. Compute and record SHA-256 checksums of every raw downloaded file in `data/raw/<name>/checksums.sha256` and reference them in the provenance `metadata.yaml` (constitution Principle III: checksummed data under `data/`; the project `state/` hash map is platform-owned and updated by the platform at verification time, not by project tasks). Handle missing values (imputation), encode categoricals, write `data/processed/<name>/train.parquet` and `holdout.parquet` with an 80/20 train/hold-out split (seed 123, per FR-015: training set for model fitting, hold-out used exclusively for fidelity evaluation) and a provenance `metadata.yaml` (checksums, imputation strategy, encoding strategy, split fraction, seed) per the data model. Enforce FR-009: monitor peak RSS; if >6.5 GB (a deliberately stricter headroom below the 7 GB hard limit, reconciling the spec's 7 GB trigger with a safety margin), uniformly down-sample to ≤10k rows or drop highest-cardinality categorical columns, logging the mitigation to `data/processed/<name>/preprocess_log.txt`. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_loader.py` checks no nulls in the training matrix, correct 80/20 split fractions, provenance metadata presence, and that recorded checksums match recomputed SHA-256 values (FR-001, FR-009, FR-015).
- [~] T002 [US2] Implement marginal and correlation fidelity metrics in `src/metrics/marginal.py` and `src/metrics/correlation.py`. Marginal: per-column mean, variance, KS statistic + p-value for continuous columns, chi-square statistic + p-value for categorical columns, KDE PDF estimates. Correlation: Pearson and Spearman matrices, absolute per-pair differences, **Fisher's z-transformed correlation deviations** (per constitution Principle VI: for each column pair, Fisher-z transform both real-hold-out and synthetic Pearson correlations via `atanh`, clipped to [-0.999, 0.999], and record the absolute z-deviation), plus a permutation-based correlation-difference test (≥1000 permutations, fixed seed). Implement FR-011: detect zero-variance synthetic columns where the real column has non-zero variance, flag as fidelity failure, skip the KS test gracefully. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_metrics.py` validates KS/chi-square/Fisher-z outputs against hand-computed values on a small real/synthetic pair from the processed Adult data (produced by T001), and confirms zero-variance handling does not crash (FR-004, FR-005, FR-011, FR-014; constitution Principle VI).
- [ ] T003 [US1] Implement the generator wrapper in `src/models/trainer.py` and synthesis in `src/models/synthesize.py` using `sdv`: CTGAN, DP-GAN (privacy budget ε=1.0, logged per FR-016), CopulaGAN, each with `max_epochs=30`, early stopping per FR-013 (validation-loss improvement <0.001 over 3 consecutive epochs — mandatory per FR-013; FR-002's "optional" wording is stale), CPU-only. Detect non-convergence/failure per FR-010: log the failure, record NaN metrics for that (model, dataset, seed), and continue. Run three seeds (42, 123, 2026) per (model, dataset) per FR-017. Generate synthetic datasets with row count matching the training split, written to `outputs/synthetic/<dataset>_<model>_seed<NN>.csv` with the JSON side-car metadata from the data model. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_trainer.py` runs one CTGAN fit for 2 epochs on down-sampled Adult (produced by T001) and checks the CSV row count and side-car fields (FR-002, FR-003, FR-010, FR-013, FR-016, FR-017).
- [ ] T004 [US1] Connect the end-to-end entry point `src/cli/run_fidelity.py` and run a thin first pass: one dataset (Adult), one model (CTGAN), one seed (42), full metric computation (including Fisher-z correlation deviations), writing real result rows to `outputs/metrics/metric_results_smoke.json` conforming to the canonical contract `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/contracts/metric_results.schema.yaml`. Document the runnable command in `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/quickstart.md`. Verify: the documented command exits 0 within the smoke budget and `pytest tests/contract/test_metric_schema.py` validates the output rows against the contract schema at the canonical path (FR-001–FR-005 partial; SC-005 partial).

**Checkpoint**: `python -m src.cli.run_fidelity --smoke` executes end-to-end on real Adult data and its numerical outputs in `outputs/metrics/metric_results_smoke.json` are schema-valid and checkable. No report writing from expected or invented results.

## Phase 2: Complete the study and validate its evidence

- [ ] T005 [US1] Execute the full training/generation grid — 3 datasets × 3 models × 3 seeds (27 runs) — via `src/cli/run_fidelity.py --full`, respecting the ≤30-epoch limit, ≤7 GB RAM monitor, and ≤6 h wall-clock budget (log per-run timings to `outputs/metrics/runtime_log.txt` for SC-005; the plan's "[deferred]" runtime estimate must be replaced by these measured timings — no unevidenced timing compliance claims). Non-convergent runs follow FR-010 (NaN metrics, continue). Verify: all 27 synthetic CSVs (or logged NaN-failure records) exist under `outputs/synthetic/`, and the runtime log confirms total wall-clock within budget (FR-002, FR-003, FR-010, FR-013, FR-017; SC-001, SC-005).
- [ ] T006 [US2] Run the full metric computation over all (dataset, model, seed) combinations and apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction across all p-values per dataset in `src/metrics/significance.py`, writing `outputs/metrics/metric_results.json` with raw p-values, corrected p-values, effect sizes, and Fisher's z-transformed correlation deviations per the contract. Verify: `pytest tests/contract/test_metric_schema.py` passes on the full results file; every continuous column has a KS row, every categorical column a ChiSquare row, and every column pair PearsonDiff/SpearmanDiff/PermutationCorr rows plus a FisherZ deviation row (constitution Principle VI) (FR-004, FR-005, FR-006).
- [ ] T007 [US3] Implement baselines and sensitivity analysis in `src/analysis/sensitivity.py`: (a) random-noise baseline sampling each column independently from the empirical hold-out marginals with seed 42 (FR-019) for SC-003 comparison; (b) control-perturbation dataset from the hold-out set with **100% of rows independently permuted within each column** (destroying all dependence structure while preserving each marginal exactly; the permutation fraction, 1.0, is recorded in the output) per FR-021; (c) faithful/unfaithful classification per FR-020: the `faithful` boolean in `metric_results.json` encodes **exactly** the FR-020 rule — corrected p ≥ 0.05 AND effect-size threshold (KS ≤ 0.1 continuous, χ² ≤ χ²₀.₉₅ categorical) — with no power condition; (d) threshold sweep {0.01, 0.05, 0.1} reporting classification stability (SC-004) and false-positive/false-negative rates against the perturbation truth set (FR-022); (e) post-hoc power estimates for KS/chi-square tests recorded in the `power_estimate` field: columns with power < 0.8 are flagged `inconclusive` in a separate supplementary column of `sensitivity_results.json` and reported in a supplementary power-filtered tally — this supplementary tally NEVER replaces the FR-020/SC-002 faithful tally, which is always reported as specified. Write results to `outputs/analysis/sensitivity_results.json` containing both the FR-020 tally and the supplementary power-filtered tally. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_sensitivity.py` checks the baseline reproduces hold-out marginals, the perturbation set (full within-column permutation) triggers expected unfaithful classifications, FP/FN rates are in [0,1], and the `faithful` field matches the FR-020 rule exactly (FR-007, FR-019, FR-020, FR-021, FR-022; SC-003, SC-004).
- [ ] T008 [US2] Implement cross-seed and cross-method aggregation in `src/analysis/report.py` (aggregation portion), consuming T007's `outputs/analysis/sensitivity_results.json` for the faithful classification: per (dataset, model, metric) mean ± SD across seeds written to `outputs/summary/aggregated_metrics.csv` (columns per data model: dataset, model, metric_type, mean_statistic, std_statistic, mean_effect_size, std_effect_size, fraction_faithful — computed with the FR-020 definition from T007), plus paired significance testing between methods (paired t-test, or Wilcoxon signed-rank when normality is rejected) on metric differences (FR-018). Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_aggregation.py` checks aggregation against manually computed means/SDs on a subset, confirms the paired-test selection logic, and confirms fraction_faithful matches the FR-020 classifications from sensitivity_results.json (FR-012, FR-017, FR-018).
- [ ] T009 [US2] Generate all visual artifacts directly from `outputs/metrics/metric_results.json` and the synthetic/hold-out data: side-by-side KDE-vs-histogram marginals, QQ-plots for continuous columns, and Pearson/Spearman correlation heatmaps (real vs synthetic) for each dataset-method pair, saved as PNGs under `outputs/figures/<dataset>_<model>_seed<NN>/`. Verify: `pytest tests/unit/test_figures.py` asserts that every `(dataset, model, seed)` directory under `outputs/figures/` contains non-empty (size > 0) KDE, QQ-plot, and correlation-heatmap PNG files, and that figure modification times post-date the metric_results.json file they are generated from (FR-014).

**Checkpoint**: All 27 runs complete; metrics, sensitivity, aggregation, and figures match the actual computations. Checks run after their prerequisites.

## Phase 3: Reproducible results and paper handoff

- [ ] T010 [US3] Generate the final report in `src/analysis/report.py`: `outputs/report/fidelity_report.json` (machine-readable tables: aggregated metrics, sensitivity sweep with FP/FN rates, power caveats, privacy budget ε=1.0 for DP-GAN per FR-016) and `outputs/report/fidelity_report.pdf` (Jinja2-rendered, matplotlib PNGs embedded). The report MUST apply and note the Benjamini-Hochberg correction, include the sensitivity analysis table over {0.01, 0.05, 0.1}, include a "Power & Equivalence" subsection reporting the supplementary power-filtered tally alongside (never instead of) the FR-020 faithful tally, and contain explicit associational framing language ("These results describe associations and distributions, not causal effects of the generators"). Verify: an inspection test asserts the presence of the sensitivity table, the multiplicity-correction note, the ε log, and the associational-framing sentence in the JSON report (FR-008, FR-016).
- [ ] T011 [US3] Write a concise methods/results account in `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/research.md` linked to the actual output cells in `outputs/metrics/metric_results.json`, `outputs/summary/aggregated_metrics.csv`, and `outputs/analysis/sensitivity_results.json`, plus the figure files. Report per-method fidelity findings (including which methods failed to converge, NaN outcomes, and any RAM-mitigation actions), negative findings, and limitations (down-sampling effects, power-constrained columns, associational scope) honestly. Verify: every numeric claim in the account traces to a named artifact file.
- [ ] T012 [US3] Re-run the documented workflow from its declared inputs (`python -m src.cli.run_fidelity --full` per `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/quickstart.md`), confirm all tests pass (`pytest tests/` including the contract test against `outputs/metrics/metric_results.json` and the canonical contract at `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/contracts/metric_results.schema.yaml`), confirm the wall-clock and RAM budgets hold (SC-001, SC-005), and document the paper-stage handoff in `specs/001-statistical-fidelity/research.md`: the paper stage must consume `outputs/report/fidelity_report.json`, `outputs/summary/aggregated_metrics.csv`, and `outputs/figures/`, and preserve the associational framing, multiplicity correction, Fisher-z reporting, and power-caveat requirements in the manuscript.
